RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is common in municipal government and is weak evidence on its own — it's a symptom of the sector's demographics more than proof of bias in your case. Leading with it makes you look like you're reaching, and it's easy to dismiss.

Your stronger facts are concrete: a credentials gap (master's plus licence versus bachelor's), twelve years of directly relevant experience, and an unanswered two-week-old request for written reasons. That last point is the lever — many jurisdictions require documented selection rationale. Send a follow-up in writing, citing any applicable policy or access-to-information route, and ask for the scoring matrix.

If the reasons come back thin or shifting, the panel composition becomes useful context. Not before.
